title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Anthropic ships the August Claude Code build — screen-reader mode, hardened background agents, corporate-proxy support, and a raft of CLI/SDK reliability + session-memory fixes
bullets.summary: The August release improves background-agent behavior and session reliability, adds accessibility and corporate process-wrapper support, and cuts memory use while fixing many CLI/SDK bugs.
bullets.how: The substrate The Construct's own operators run on: more reliable background agents and durable sessions harden long-running scheduled operators like this Pulse job, and corporate-proxy support lets us run the same stack inside a client's network.

bullets.title: Claude Code's /usage now attributes MCP-server cost correctly — a server's share reflects only the requests that actually consumed its tool results
bullets.summary: The overattribution bug that inflated per-server usage is fixed, so cost/latency now maps cleanly to the specific tool that produced results.
bullets.how: Real per-server observability is the cost-accounting layer The Construct needs to price governed operators per client: prove which MCP server drove which spend and you can bill orchestration as a metered product instead of a flat retainer.

bullets.title: Claude Cowork now runs remote background sessions on web + mobile (beta) — server-side files and session state, scheduled tasks that run with no device online
bullets.summary: Sessions and file state persist to your Claude account and keep running detached from any one machine, synced across desktop/web/phone.
bullets.how: Directly upgrades how The Construct's scheduled operators run: detached, durable, resumable across devices, so long-running agent work no longer depends on a laptop staying awake — the reliability floor under the whole scheduled-agent fleet.

bullets.title: Pipedrive's native MCP server makes the SDR-first CRM fully agent-callable — search deals, create records, update contacts, schedule activities, automate pipeline from any MCP client
bullets.summary: Natural-language read/write over the full CRM surface from Claude/ChatGPT, aimed at high-velocity sales teams; the pipeline-first entrant alongside HubSpot and Salesforce MCPs.
bullets.how: Completes the CRM-tier map for Hartley/PRAGMA deal-ops (Salesforce=enterprise, HubSpot=mid-market, Pipedrive=SDR); The Construct's move is one revenue-ops operator that routes across whichever CRM MCP the client already runs, owning the workflow above all three.

bullets.title: arXiv 'Reinforcement Learning for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems through Orchestration Traces' (2605.02801) — treats spawn/delegate/return/aggregate/stop as a learnable temporal graph, flags the stopping decision as untrained
bullets.summary: Frames a whole multi-agent run as an orchestration trace you can optimize, not a pile of isolated calls, and identifies the stopping decision as the piece with no explicit RL method yet.
bullets.how: A direct architecture pointer for The Construct's operator hierarchies: instrument every sub-agent spawn/delegation/stop as a trace so we can measure and tune where hierarchies over-run or under-delegate — the knob that decides whether deep operators are cheap or ruinous.

praxis_lesson: Frontier held today (GPT-5.6 Jul 9, Gemini 3.6 Flash Jul 21 still newest), so the real signal is substrate reliability and cost-attribution, not new weights — the August Claude Code build hardens background agents and durable sessions while /usage finally maps spend to the exact MCP server that earned it. That combination turns a scheduled agent fleet from a demo into a billable product: The Construct's edge is a governed, observable, per-server-metered orchestration layer that keeps running detached across devices and can prove which tool drove which dollar.
